producer_report.summary: I moved the two test modules, `critic_soundness_tests` and `produce_and_verify_order_tests`, from run/mod.rs into a new run/tests.rs. mod.rs now declares `#[cfg(test)] mod tests;`. The moved text is byte-identical except the `use super::*;` line in each module, which is now `use super::super::*;`. The `check_seam` test seam stays in mod.rs because production code in checks.rs reads it. Callers keep their `run::` paths, and I added an R9 entry to CHANGELOG.md. fmt and clippy pass, and the 21 moved tests pass under `run::tests::`. I did not run the full suite or diff the before and after test lists name by name, so those are left to Athena's checks. In my snapshot `cargo test -p xtask --test policy` fails one test, because it reads only tracked files and tests.rs is still untracked. The three test names it reports are defined in tests.rs.

11 of 12 pass. every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists fails only because the new tests.rs is untracked and the scan reads tracked files. The three names it reports are defined in tests.rs lines 333, 363, 390. It should pass once the file is tracked.

open_issues: The policy test every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists fails in my snapshot only because tests.rs is untracked. It should pass in the candidate.
The `#[cfg(test)]` attributes on the two modules inside tests.rs are redundant, since `mod tests;` already carries it. I kept them so the text stays identical.
mistakes: I could not diff the full before and after --list outputs by name, because the saved output lies outside the working directory. Athena's full test run should confirm the count.
learnings: xtask policy tests scan only tracked files, so a new untracked .rs file makes every_test_named_in_the_enforcement_map_exists fail until it is tracked.
Test names appear in docs/enforcement.md. A test that is moved must stay defined somewhere in a tracked .rs file.
Moving the test modules one level deeper into tests.rs required `use super::super::*;` in each, to reach run's private imports.
desires: A way to copy line ranges without a script. I used a temporary Cargo program and deleted it afterwards.
